lessons.en: The alphabet and where sounds are made
lessons.b:
Sanskrit has 13 vowels (अच्) and 33 consonants (हल्), plus anusvāra (ं) and visarga (ः). Every sound has a place (स्थानम्) and an effort (प्रयत्नः). The grammar uses these to decide which sounds are "similar" (सवर्ण) — the basis of most sandhi rules.

lessons.en: Śiva-sūtras and the short-hand names for sound groups
lessons.b: Pāṇini lists the sounds in fourteen Māheśvara-sūtras. Each ends in a marker consonant (इत्). A pratyāhāra — a first sound plus a later marker — names every sound in between: अच् = all vowels, हल् = all consonants, इक् = इ उ ऋ ऌ, यण् = य व र ल. Try any pratyāhāra below.

lessons.en: Key terms: it, guṇa, vṛddhi, saṃyoga, pada …
lessons.b:
The grammar works with defined terms (संज्ञा). The ones you meet in every derivation:

  • इत् — a marker letter that is dropped (1.3.2–9); it switches rules on: कित् blocks guṇa, णित्/ञित् bring vṛddhi.
  • वृद्धिः = आ ऐ औ (1.1.1); गुणः = अ ए ओ (1.1.2) — the two vowel grades.
  • संयोगः — a consonant cluster (1.1.7). पदम् — a word ending in sup or tiṅ (1.4.14). धातुः — a root (1.3.1). प्रातिपदिकम् — a noun stem (1.2.45–46).
  • सार्वधातुकम् / आर्धधातुकम् — the two kinds of verbal suffix (3.4.113–114) that decide vikaraṇa and iṭ.

When a word ends in a vowel and the next begins with one, they combine. Five rules do almost all the work: सवर्णदीर्घः (like + like → long), गुणः (a + i/u/ṛ → e/o/ar), वृद्धिः (a + e/o → ai/au), यण् (i/u/ṛ + unlike vowel → y/v/r), अयादिः (e/o/ai/au + vowel → ay/av/āy/āv) — and पूर्वरूपम् (e/o + a → e/o + ऽ).

A final consonant takes on the voice of what follows (जश्त्वम्: वाक् + ईशः → वागीशः), assimilates (तत् + च → तच्च, तत् + लयः → तल्लयः), or a final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant. Visarga becomes ओ after अ before soft sounds (रामः + गच्छति → रामो गच्छति), श्/स् before च/त, र् after other vowels, or drops.

lessons.en: Nouns: eight cases, three numbers, three genders
lessons.b: A noun stem (प्रातिपदिकम्) takes one of the 21 sup endings (सु औ जस् …) for 7 cases × 3 numbers, plus the vocative. Each case expresses a kāraka role: प्रथमा the subject, द्वितीया the object, तृतीया the instrument, चतुर्थी the recipient, पञ्चमी the source, षष्ठी relation, सप्तमी location. Start with राम — the model for every a-stem masculine noun.

lessons.en: Vowel stems in the three genders
lessons.b: The ending of the stem and its gender decide the pattern. Learn one model for each: राम (अ पुं), रमा (आ स्त्री), वन (अ नपुं), हरि, मति, वारि (इ), गुरु, धेनु, मधु (उ), नदी (ई), वधू (ऊ), पितृ, मातृ, दातृ (ऋ).

Consonant stems change their stem before different endings: राजन् → राजा, राजानम्, राज्ञा; मनस् → मनः, मनसा; भगवत् → भगवान्, भगवन्तम्; वाच् → वाक्, वाचा. The "strong" stem appears in the first five endings (सर्वनामस्थानम्, 1.1.43).

Pronouns (सर्वादि गण, 1.1.27) have their own endings — सर्वे not सर्वाः, सर्वस्मै not सर्वाय. तद् (स, सा, तत्), यद्, किम्, इदम्, अदस्, and the personal pronouns अस्मद् (अहम्) and युष्मद् (त्वम्), which have no gender. Numerals एक–चतुर् agree in gender; पञ्चन् onwards do not.

lessons.en: Verbs: person, number, the present tense
lessons.b: A verb = root (धातुः) + vikaraṇa + one of 18 tiṅ endings: 3 persons (प्रथम = he/she, मध्यम = you, उत्तम = I/we) × 3 numbers × 2 padas (परस्मैपदम्, आत्मनेपदम्). लट् is the present: भवति "is, becomes". Click any form to watch the rules build it: भू + लट् → तिप् → शप् → गुणः → अवादेशः → भवति.

Roots marked with an anudātta vowel or ङ् take ātmanepada (एधते, सेवते); those marked with svarita or ञ् take both (करोति / कुरुते, "does for others / for oneself"); the rest take parasmaipada. Upasargas can change the pada: नि + विश् → निविशते (1.3.17).

lessons.en: The ten classes and their stem-suffixes
lessons.b: Before sārvadhātuka endings each class inserts its own vikaraṇa: भ्वादि शप् (भवति), अदादि — (अत्ति), जुहोत्यादि श्लु + reduplication (जुहोति), दिवादि श्यन् (दीव्यति), स्वादि श्नु (सुनोति), तुदादि श (तुदति), रुधादि श्नम् (रुणद्धि), तनादि उ (तनोति), क्र्यादि श्ना (क्रीणाति), चुरादि णिच् (चोरयति).

लट् present · लिट् perfect (बभूव) · लुट् periphrastic future (भविता) · लृट् future (भविष्यति) · लोट् imperative (भवतु) · लङ् imperfect (अभवत्) · विधिलिङ् optative (भवेत्) · आशीर्लिङ् benedictive (भूयात्) · लुङ् aorist (अभूत्) · लृङ् conditional (अभविष्यत्). (लेट् is Vedic.) Past tenses लङ्, लुङ्, लृङ् take the augment अट् (6.4.71).

In the passive the object becomes the subject and the verb takes ātmanepada with the vikaraṇa यक्: रामः ग्रन्थं पठति → रामेण ग्रन्थः पठ्यते. Intransitive roots form the impersonal (भावे): मया भूयते "it is been by me".

Some suffixes make a new root from a root: णिच् "cause to" (भावयति, पाठयति), सन् "wish to" (बुभूषति, पिपठिषति), यङ् "do intensely/repeatedly" (बोभूयते). These new roots take every lakāra — open them in धातुरूपाणि with the सनादि menu.

प्र परा अप सम् अनु अव निस् दुस् वि आङ् नि अधि अपि अति सु उद् अभि प्रति परि उप. "An upasarga forcibly carries the root's meaning elsewhere": हरति takes, प्रहरति strikes, आहरति brings, संहरति destroys, विहरति roams, परिहरति avoids. See them all live on the प्रत्ययाः · उपसर्गाः page.

lessons.en: Primary derivatives: participles, gerunds, infinitives, agent and action nouns
lessons.b: Suffixes added directly to roots: गतः (क्त), गतवान् (क्तवतु), गच्छन् (शतृ), गत्वा (क्त्वा), आगम्य (ल्यप्), गन्तुम् (तुमुन्), गन्तव्यः (तव्य), गमनीयः (अनीयर्), गमनम् (ल्युट्), गन्तृ (तृच्), गामकः (ण्वुल्), गतिः (क्तिन्). Participles decline like nouns.

Suffixes added to nouns: दाशरथिः "son of Daśaratha" (इञ्), औपगवः (अण्), देवत्वम् / देवता "divinity" (त्व, तल्), शिववान् "having Śiva" (मतुप्), पटुतरः / पटीयान् "cleverer", पटुतमः / पटिष्ठः "cleverest", सुवर्णमयम् "made of gold" (मयट्), तत्र "there" (त्रल्).
Feminines are made with टाप् (अज → अजा, बाल → बाला), ङीप् (कर्तृ → कर्त्री, भवत् → भवती), ङीष् (गौर → गौरी), ति (युवन् → युवतिः), ऊङ् (कुरु → कुरूः).

Two or more words join into one; the case endings inside drop (2.4.71) and the compound is explained by a vigraha:

समासःexamplevigraha
अव्ययीभावः (2.1.5)यथाशक्तिशक्तिम् अनतिक्रम्य — first member an indeclinable; the whole is indeclinable
तत्पुरुषः (2.1.22)राजपुरुषःराज्ञः पुरुषः — the second member is the head; named by the case of the first: द्वितीया (कृष्णाश्रितः), तृतीया (शङ्कुलाखण्डः), चतुर्थी (यूपदारु), पञ्चमी (चोरभयम्), षष्ठी (राजपुरुषः), सप्तमी (अक्षशौण्डः)
कर्मधारयः (1.2.42)नीलोत्पलम्नीलं च तत् उत्पलं च — both members refer to the same thing
द्विगुः (2.1.52)त्रिलोकीत्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः — first member a numeral
नञ्तत्पुरुषः (2.2.6)अब्राह्मणःन ब्राह्मणः
बहुव्रीहिः (2.2.24)पीताम्बरःपीतम् अम्बरं यस्य सः (विष्णुः) — the compound describes something else
द्वन्द्वः (2.2.29)रामलक्ष्मणौ · पाणिपादम्रामः च लक्ष्मणः च — "and"; इतरेतर (dual/plural) or समाहार (neuter singular)

Compounds are analysed by meaning, so they are taught here with models rather than generated.

Words that never change (1.1.37): च, वा, हि, तु, एव, अपि, इति, न, यथा, तथा, यदा, तदा, कदा, अत्र, तत्र, कुत्र, सह, विना, उच्चैः, नीचैः, शनैः… Also the forms in -त्वा, -तुम्, -य (1.1.39–40) and taddhitas like -तः, -त्र, -दा (1.1.38).

lessons.en: Kārakas: how cases show roles in a sentence
lessons.b: Pāṇini defines six kārakas by their part in the action: अपादानम् fixed point of departure (1.4.24 → पञ्चमी: वृक्षात् पत्रं पतति), सम्प्रदानम् recipient (1.4.32 → चतुर्थी: विप्राय गां ददाति), करणम् chief means (1.4.42 → तृतीया: दात्रेण लुनाति), अधिकरणम् locus (1.4.45 → सप्तमी: स्थाल्यां पचति), कर्म what the agent most wants (1.4.49 → द्वितीया: कटं करोति), कर्ता the independent agent (1.4.54). The case appears only on the kāraka that the verb does not already express (2.3.1 अनभिहिते).

Verse is measured by syllable weight: a syllable is गुरु if its vowel is long or it is followed by a cluster, anusvāra or visarga; otherwise लघु. Metres are defined by gaṇas of three syllables (य मा ता रा ज भा न स ल गम्) or by mātrās (āryā). Find the metre of any verse in the metre finder, and practise in the game.
